findings.title: New parsers verified against the real CLI output shapes
findings.description: The three new consumers of production JSON were checked against the producers: `purchase_accounting.accounting_rows` reads exactly the keys `accounting_futures._product_payload` emits (`families[]` from `jsonable(asdict(TickAccountingLine))`, `cross_tier` as a list of `CrossTierResult` dicts keyed `check/agree/under/over/no_trades`); `check_dataset_edge` reads `products[].edge_available_end` which `TickStatus.to_dict` renders via `jsonable` as an aware-UTC ISO instant; `not_caught_up_report` reads `products[].sessions[].{session_date,status,unit_ids}` plus per-document `volume_checks` as `TickCoverage.to_dict` emits them, and its status buckets exactly cover the `TickSessionStatus` members (with an explicit stop on an unknown bucket). `FetchStatus` comparisons use the uppercase stored values that `debug_reads` round-trips. No mismatch found.

findings.title: `EXIT_USAGE = 2` is dead code
findings.description: The constant added in this diff is never referenced anywhere in the file: argparse's exit code is returned via `return int(exc.code or 0)` in `main`, and `test_no_argument_prints_usage_and_exits_two` asserts the literal `2`. It looks like a leftover from an earlier design where `main` returned the constant explicitly. Delete it or use it in the `SystemExit` handler.

findings.title: The `mt data tick` exit-code vocabulary exists in two places
findings.description: `cutover_304_evidence.py` still hardcodes `EXIT_OK, EXIT_PARTIAL = 0, 3` (pre-existing line), while the new `scripts/purchase_verdicts.py` imports the same values canonically from `manta_trading.cli.commands.tick_exit` (`STATUS_ACCEPTED_EXITS = (EXIT_OK, EXIT_PARTIAL)`). AGENTS.md asks that a comparison value used in conditionals be defined once; now a change to the CLI's exit contract requires editing the evidence script by hand. Switching `cutover_304_evidence.py` to the shared import would collapse the two sources.

findings.title: A `TypeError` from naive/aware timestamp comparison would escape `main`'s catch list
findings.description: `resubmit_origins` guards only the `datetime.fromisoformat` call; the later `made < since` comparison (and `judge`'s parse of the start file) can raise `TypeError` if one side is offset-naive. I verified the production path is safe — `tick_request.requested_at` is a timestamptz rendered by `_cell` as an aware ISO instant, and the start file is written with `datetime.now(UTC).isoformat()` — but `main` catches `(CutoverError, CalledProcessError, OSError)` and `(KeyError, ValueError)`, not `TypeError`, so a hand-edited start file or a future schema change would produce a bare traceback instead of the narrated `FAILED:` line every other stop gets. Adding `TypeError` to the payload-stop clause (or normalizing to UTC with an explicit check) would keep the stop in the record.
